notesStmt.note: The note at the bottom of this manuscript is a rare instance of Whitman's providing an exact (and reliable) date: the evening of January 4, 1891.
"The Pallid Wreath" was published in the 10 January 1891 issue of the Critic and reprinted in Good–Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.head: The Pallid wreath.
lg.l: Somehow I cannot let it go yet, ‸funereal tho' it is,
Let it remain back there on its nail suspended,

With pink, blue, yellow, ‸all blanch'd, and the white
now gray and ashy,
One wither'd rose put ‸years ago for thee, dear friend,
But I do not forget thee. Hast thou then faded?
Is the odor exhaled? Are the colors, vitalities, dead?

No, while memories subtly play—the past vivid
as ever;

For but last night I woke and in that spectral
ring saw thee,
Thy smile, eyes, face, calm, silent, loving as ever:

No ‸So let the wreath hang yet still awhile within my
eye⹀reach,
It is not yet dead ‸to me or even pallid.
